source_text: Sententia tenetur, et quantum audiuimus ab ipso fratre nostro, quem deus faciat pacatum fratrem nostrum, ab isto Emerito est dicta sententia ubi illi damnati sunt. legatur ipsa sententia ubi illi damnati sunt, et legatur sententia ubi Caecilianum damnauerunt maiores istorum, et uideamus qui rei peiores facti sunt, qui grauiore sententia puniti, qui strepitu maiore damnati. ibi dixit: licet enim uiperei seminis noxios partus uenenati uteri alueus diu texerit et concepti sceleris uda coagula in aspidum membra tardo se calore uaporauerint, tamen conceptum uirus euanescente umbraculo occultari non potuit. nam etsi sero publicum tamen parricidium et facinus suum feta scelerum uota pepererunt, quod ante praedictum est: \'parturiit iniustitiam, concepit dolorem et peperit iniquitatem.\' sed quoniam serenum iam fulget e nubilo nec est confusa criminum silua, cum ad poenam designata sunt nomina — indulgentia enim antehac fuerat —, dum clementiae dimittimus lineam, inuenit causa quos puniat. et inter cetera: loquamur, carissimi fratres, schismatis causas, quia iam non possumus tacere personas. Maximianum fidei aemulum, ueritatis adulterum, ecclesiae matris inimicum, Dathae, Chorae et Abiron ministrum. haec uerba sunt partis Donati in Maximianistas isto ut audiuimus dictante prolata. scitis autem qui sunt Dathan, Chore et Abiron. ipsi primo schisma fecerunt, quibus poena usitata non suffecit: uiuos aperta terra deuorauit. Dathae, Chorae et Abiron ministrum, uerba ipsius sunt, de pacis gremio sententiae fulmen excussit. audite adhuc: et quod adhuc eum, inquit, dehiscens terra non absorbuit, ad maius iudicium superis reseruauit. raptus enim poenam sui compendio lucrauerat funeris; usuras nunc grauioris colligit faenoris, cum mortuus interest uiuis. uerba sunt ipsius Maximianum damnantis uel potius, ut ipse dicit, \'ore ueridico\' fulminantis. et tamen collecti sunt, aspides uiperae parricidae nec exsufflatur baptismus, quem dedit aspis uipera parricida. audistis, quantus ignis exarserit eloquentiae, quando inuenit faenum quod posset incendere. frater Emerite, amplexus es fratrem tuum Felicianum tui oris fulmine condemnatum: agnosce fratrem tuum Deuterium tibi etiam genere sociatum.
thought_title: Emeritus's own sentence against the Maximianists is read back
orientation: Augustine is speaking to the gathered church, asking that the sentence by which Emeritus condemned the Maximianists be read aloud, and then comparing it with the sentence by which the Donatists' predecessors condemned Caecilian.
pass_a_gloss: The sentence is held, and as much as we heard from our brother himself, whom God may make a peaceable brother of ours, by this Emeritus the sentence was spoken where those men were condemned. Let the sentence itself be read where those men were condemned, and let the sentence be read where the ancestors of these men condemned Caecilian, and let us see who were made the worse defendants, who were punished with a heavier sentence, who were condemned with greater uproar. There he said: for although the harmful offspring of viper seed the channel of the poisoned womb long covered and the wet curdlings of conceived crime warmed themselves into the limbs of asps with slow heat, yet the conceived poison could not be hidden when the shade vanished. For although late, yet the public parricide and their crime the pregnant vows of crimes brought forth, which was foretold before: 'she travailed with injustice, conceived pain and brought forth iniquity.' But since the calm now shines from the cloud and the forest of crimes is not confused, when the names are marked out for punishment — for there had been indulgence before — while we let out the line of clemency, the case finds whom it may punish. And among other things: let us speak, dearest brothers, of the causes of the schism, because we can no longer be silent about the persons. Maximianus, rival of the faith, adulterer of the truth, enemy of the mother church, minister of Dathan, Korah and Abiram. These words are of the Donatist party against the Maximianists, brought forth, as we heard, with this man dictating. But you know who Dathan, Korah and Abiram are. They first made a schism, for whom the usual punishment was not enough: the open earth devoured them alive. Minister of Dathan, Korah and Abiram, the words are his own, from the bosom of peace he hurled the thunderbolt of the sentence. Hear still more: and because, he says, the gaping earth did not yet swallow him, he reserved him for a greater judgment above. For snatched away, he would have gained the penalty of his own funeral as a shortcut; now he collects the interest of a heavier loan, since dead he is present among the living. The words are his own condemning Maximianus, or rather, as he himself says, thundering with 'truth-speaking mouth.' And yet they were gathered together, asps, vipers, parricides, and the baptism is not blown upon, which the asp, viper, parricide gave. You heard how great a fire of eloquence blazed up, when it found hay that it could set on fire. Brother Emeritus, you have embraced your brother Felicianus condemned by the thunderbolt of your mouth: acknowledge your brother Deuterius joined to you even by family.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the passive; Augustine is saying the sentence is available or on record, not that it is being physically held.

choices.term: uiperei seminis noxios partus uenenati uteri alueus diu texerit
choices.english: the harmful offspring of viper seed the channel of the poisoned womb long covered
choices.why: Keeps the dense, ugly word order and the metaphor of the womb as a channel or bed; 'noxios partus' is rendered as 'harmful offspring' to preserve the plural force.
rejected: the poisonous offspring of viper seed lay long hidden in the channel of the envenomed womb

choices.why: Literal for the thick, clotted matter of conceived crime; 'curdlings' preserves the physical, unpleasant image.
Keeps the metaphor of vows as pregnant and giving birth; 'feta' is literally 'pregnant' or 'having brought forth.'

choices.english: while we let out the line of clemency
choices.why: Preserves the fishing or measuring metaphor of 'linea' as a line let out; 'dimittimus' is literally 'we send away' or 'let out.'
rejected: while we extend the line of mercy
while we grant a measure of clemency

choices.why: Literal rendering of the compound adjective; Augustine is quoting Emeritus's own self-description, so the oddity is kept.

bible_refs.note: parturiit iniustitiam, concepit dolorem et peperit iniquitatem

pass_b_english: The sentence is held, and as we heard from our brother himself—may God make him our peaceful brother—this sentence by which they were condemned was spoken by Emeritus here. Let the very sentence by which they were condemned be read, and let the sentence by which their ancestors condemned Caecilian be read, and let us see which men were made the worse criminals, which were punished with a heavier sentence, which were condemned with greater uproar. There he said: 'For although the channel of the poisoned womb long covered the harmful offspring of viper seed, and the wet curdlings of conceived crime warmed into the limbs of asps with slow heat, yet the conceived venom could not be hidden once the shadow was gone. For although late, still the parricide and its crime were brought to public birth by the vows pregnant with crimes, as was foretold: "She travailed with injustice, conceived pain, and gave birth to iniquity" (Psalm 7:14). But since the clear sky now shines from the cloud and the forest of crimes is no longer tangled, when the names have been marked out for punishment—for there had been indulgence before—while we let out the line of clemency, the case finds whom to punish.' And among other things: 'Let us speak, dearest brothers, of the causes of the schism, because we can no longer keep silent about the persons. Maximianus, rival of the faith, corrupter of the truth, enemy of mother church, minister of Dathan, Korah and Abiram.' These are the words of the Donatist party against the Maximianists, brought forth, as we heard, with this man dictating. You know who Dathan, Korah and Abiram are. They first made a schism, and the usual punishment was not enough for them: the open earth devoured them alive. 'Minister of Dathan, Korah and Abiram'—these are his own words—he hurled the thunderbolt of a sentence from the bosom of peace. Listen further: 'And because the gaping earth did not swallow him too,' he says, 'it reserved him for a greater judgment above. For snatched away, he had gained the penalty of his own death prematurely; now he collects the interest of a heavier debt, since dead he is present among the living.' These are his own words condemning Maximianus, or rather, as he himself says, thundering with a 'truth-speaking mouth.' And yet they were received back—asps, vipers, parricides—and the baptism given by an asp, a viper, a parricide is not exsufflated. You heard how great a fire of eloquence blazed up when it found straw it could burn. Brother Emeritus, you embraced your brother Felicianus, condemned by the thunderbolt of your own mouth: acknowledge your brother Deuterius, joined to you even by family.

problems.why: rei here means 'guilty/criminals,' not 'defendants' in a legal sense; the comparison is about who were made worse criminals.
problems.fix: which men were made the worse criminals
problems.ruling: 'rei' means guilty/criminals here, not 'defendants'; meaning is changed.

problems.quote: seized, he had gained the penalty of his own death as a bargain
problems.source_quote: raptus enim poenam sui compendio lucrauerat funeris
problems.why: compendio means 'saving/gain by abbreviation,' i.e., he got off lightly by dying quickly; 'bargain' is wrong. 'By a shortcut' or 'cheaply'—he escaped worse punishment by dying first.
problems.fix: for seized, he had gained the penalty of his death cheaply
problems.ruling: 'bargain' for compendio misses sense of escaping lightly by quick death; misleading.

problems.quote: since dead he is present among the living
problems.why: interest here means 'he is at stake/is liable for/is charged against,' not 'is present among'; the dead man is held accountable by the living.
problems.fix: since dead he is held accountable by the living
problems.ruling: 'interest uiuis' means 'matters to/concerns the living,' not 'present among'; meaning changed.

problems.why: In context, this refers to the Maximianists being received back into communion, not just 'gathered in'; the technical sense of reception is lost.
problems.ruling: 'collecti sunt' means received back into communion here, not merely gathered; misleading.

edits.old: which men were made worse defendants
edits.new: which men were made the worse criminals

edits.old: For seized, he had gained the penalty of his own death as a bargain
edits.new: For seized, he had gained the penalty of his own death cheaply

edits.old: since dead he is present among the living
edits.new: since dead he is held accountable by the living

edits.old: And yet they were gathered in—asps, vipers, parricides—
edits.new: And yet they were received back—asps, vipers, parricides—

fixed: rei peiores facti sunt: rei means guilty/criminals, not defendants; changed to 'the worse criminals'.
compendio lucrauerat funeris: compendio means by a shortcut/cheaply, not a bargain; changed to 'cheaply'.
cum mortuus interest uiuis: interest means is held accountable/liable, not is present among; changed to 'held accountable by the living'.
collecti sunt: refers to being received back into communion, not merely gathered in; changed to 'received back'.

problems.quote: since dead he is held accountable by the living
problems.why: 'Interest' means 'he is present/attends' (as in legal context), not 'is held accountable'—the point is the dead man is present among the living at judgment, not that they judge him.
problems.fix: since dead he is present among the living

problems.why: 'Feta' means pregnant/bearing, but modifies 'uota' (vows)—the phrase means 'vows pregnant with crimes' or 'crime-laden vows', not 'vows of crimes'.
problems.fix: the vows pregnant with crimes brought to public birth
problems.ruling: 'feta scelerum uota' = vows pregnant with crimes; 'pregnant vows of crimes' shifts modifier to wrong noun, misleading.

problems.quote: seized, he had gained the penalty of his own death cheaply
problems.source_quote: raptus enim poenam sui compendio lucrauerat funeris
problems.why: 'Raptus' here means 'snatched away' (by death/taken prematurely), not 'seized' (captured); 'compendio' means 'prematurely/early' (compendiously), not 'cheaply'.
problems.fix: for snatched away, he had gained the penalty of his own death prematurely
problems.ruling: 'compendio' = at a saving/cheaply, not 'prematurely'; 'raptus' = snatched away, not 'seized'; meaning distorted.

edits.old: since dead he is held accountable by the living
edits.new: since dead he is present among the living

edits.old: For seized, he had gained the penalty of his own death cheaply
edits.new: For snatched away, he had gained the penalty of his own death prematurely

fixed: Changed 'held accountable by the living' to 'present among the living' to match 'interest uiuis' (he is present among the living).
Changed 'pregnant vows of crimes' to 'vows pregnant with crimes' to match 'feta scelerum uota' (vows pregnant with crimes).
Changed 'seized...cheaply' to 'snatched away...prematurely' to match 'raptus...compendio' (snatched away...prematurely).

last_rejected.why: Augustine means from the very seat of peace, i.e. the Donatists' own peaceful communion, not a generic 'bosom of peace.'
last_rejected.fix: from the very bosom of peace
last_rejected.ruling: 'Bosom of peace' is normal range for 'pacis gremio'; no meaning changed or reader misled.

last_rejected.source_quote: parturiit iniustitiam, concepit dolorem et peperit iniquitatem
last_rejected.why: This is Psalm 7:15 (LXX/Vulgate 7:15, Hebrew 7:14). The Septuagint numbering differs; should be Psalm 7:15 with note, or standard Hebrew Psalm 7:14.
last_rejected.ruling: Psalm 7:14 is standard Hebrew numbering for this verse; numbering convention is not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: condemned by the thunderbolt of your own mouth
last_rejected.why: 'tui oris' means 'of your mouth' (genitive), but 'fulmine' is ablative of means, not genitive. The thunderbolt comes from Emeritus's mouth, not condemns him by his own mouth.
last_rejected.fix: condemned by the thunderbolt from your mouth
last_rejected.ruling: 'tui oris fulmine' = by the thunderbolt of your mouth; English correctly renders ablative means and genitive.

last_rejected.quote: joined to you even by family
last_rejected.why: 'etiam' means 'also/even,' but 'genere sociatum' means 'joined by birth/race/family.' The point is Deuterius is joined to Emeritus by family ties too, not that he is 'even' joined by family as an additional point.
last_rejected.fix: joined to you by family as well
last_rejected.ruling: 'etiam' = even/also; 'joined to you even by family' correctly captures the additional family bond.
